topics.title: Lyme and arthritis
topics.summary: The most common late manifestation of Lyme disease. Centers on the two-phase model: antibiotic-responsive infectious synovitis vs. antibiotic-refractory, post-infectious autoimmunity (identified autoantigens ECGF, Annexin A2), set against the minority persistence hypothesis.

topics.title: Lyme and Morgellons
topics.summary: A contested condition framed by mainstream medicine as delusional infestation (CDC study: textile-cellulose fibers) versus the minority 'filamentous borrelial dermatitis' hypothesis (Middelveen & Stricker: endogenous keratin/collagen filaments). Hinges on one unreplicated material-science fact.

topics.title: Lyme, Morgellons, and amphetamines
topics.summary: Stimulant-induced formication / delusional infestation ('meth mites') as the primary differential and likely subgroup explanation for Morgellons, with harm-reduction framing and a striking attribution gap between drug and infection communities for an identical symptom.

topics.title: Lyme and OCD
topics.summary: Neuropsychiatric Lyme and whether Borrelia can trigger OCD via the infection-induced autoimmune basal-ganglia mechanism established for streptococcus (PANDAS/PANS). Mechanism mainstream; Borrelia-specific causation speculative; directionality confound central.

topics.title: Lyme and parasitic infections
topics.summary: Mainstream Babesia co-infection (more severe, longer illness; often the real cause of 'treatment-resistant Lyme') cleanly separated from the minority MSIDS multi-co-infection model and fringe novel-parasite / 'rope worm' claims. Diagnostic validity is the fault line.

topics.title: Lyme, parasitic co-infection, and suicide
topics.summary: A public-health question: does tick-borne infection elevate suicide risk above the chronic-illness baseline? Mechanism (inflammation/kynurenine/quinolinic acid) is mainstream; Bransfield's infection-specific magnitude is minority-research. Two additive routes: biological and psychosocial (invalidation).

topics.title: Lyme, HIV, and syphilis
topics.summary: Spirochetal homology and the 'great imitator' parallel, Borrelia-Treponema serologic cross-reactivity (false-positive syphilis tests), and HIV effects on Lyme diagnosis/course. The syphilis analogy is chronic-Lyme advocacy's rhetorical backbone.

topics.title: Lyme, HIV, syphilis, and white blood cell disruption
topics.summary: How each pathogen perturbs leukocytes: Borrelia's humoral suppression and defective germinal centers, Borrelia-driven cutaneous B-cell lymphoma (regresses on antibiotics), HIV CD4 depletion. The minority CD57 biomarker is unvalidated; immune disruption is the project's mechanistic spine.

topics.title: Lyme as a bioweapon
topics.summary: Separates documented history (US Cold War tick-weaponization research; Burgdorfer's classified work; 2019 DoD-IG amendment) from the speculative 'escape' thesis. Ancient-DNA evidence (Otzi, 15-My amber) refutes an engineered organism; ecology explains the epidemic.

topics.title: Chronic and late-stage Lyme
topics.summary: The project's keystone controversy. Separates three things routinely merged: recognized late disseminated Lyme; recognized Post-Treatment Lyme Disease Syndrome (PTLDS, ~10-20% of treated patients, real but post-infectious); and the contested 'chronic Lyme disease' label (ongoing infection treatable with prolonged antibiotics). The illness is real; the persistent-active-infection mechanism is unproven; controlled trials show no durable benefit from long antibiotics.

topics.title: How Lyme is transmitted (tick, congenital, sexual)
topics.summary: Beyond the established tick-bite route: can Lyme pass in utero or sexually? Mainstream accepts the spirochete can rarely cross the placenta (documented since 1985) but rejects a defined congenital syndrome (removed from ICD-11) and sexual transmission. The congenital-syphilis analogy makes the vertical question scientifically serious; divergent transmission biology limits it. A missing tick-bite history is normal, not evidence of an exotic route.

topics.title: Lyme and vaccines (incl. COVID-19 vaccines)
topics.summary: Do vaccines, especially COVID-19 vaccines, activate or worsen Lyme? The strongest science is historical: the LYMErix OspA vaccine and the OspA-LFA-1 molecular-mimicry hypothesis (the same axis as Topic 1) — but the trial showed no increased arthritis and withdrawal was a media/litigation cascade, not proven harm; VLA15 now engineers out the epitope. Non-specific immune activation can flare chronic illness, and post-vaccination syndrome is a serious but preliminary research question (Yale LISTEN), yet there is no established evidence COVID vaccines reactivate Borrelia, and COVID infection is the larger, often-ignored confounder. A high-misinformation area handled with care.
